page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. This KVM-hypervised instance features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the ecs.se1ne.xlarge delivers modest performance across compute and memory subsystems. The single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU benchmarks place the instance in the bottom 25% of tested hardware, with a Passmark CPU score of 3601.23. Memory bandwidth tests show a significant drop-off from 163.7 GB/sec for cached small-block reads to 19.6 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads, which is categorized in the bottom 10%. Similarly, database operations and static web serving throughput fall into the bottom 10% tier, reflecting potential bottlenecks in high-throughput scenarios.

From a resource density perspective, this instance offers a memory-optimized profile without the premium cost of high-end compute hardware. However, the tradeoff is lower processing efficiency, as evidenced by weak performance in compression, software compilation, and LLM inference tasks. The ecs.se1ne.xlarge is best suited for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high CPU throughput, such as caching layers, lightweight database hosting, or memory-bound general-purpose applications with moderate network demands.
